RECREATIONAL.gov_quote: New Hampshire's Therapeutic Cannabis Program exempts qualifying therapeutic use from criminal penalties. Adult-use possession is not part of that exemption.
RECREATIONAL.validation_notes: Live audit on 2026-09-09 found gov_section verbatim on https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/programs-services/population-health/therapeutic-cannabis.
RECREATIONAL.question: Is it legal for adults to possess cannabis in the state of New Hampshire?
RECREATIONAL.gov_section: The Therapeutic Cannabis Program was established in 2013, under RSA 126-X. That law establishes exemptions from criminal penalties for the therapeutic use of cannabis in New Hampshire.

MEDICAL.gov_quote: Qualifying patients may possess up to two ounces of therapeutic cannabis.
MEDICAL.validation_notes: Live audit on 2026-09-09 found gov_section verbatim on https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/programs-services/population-health/therapeutic-cannabis.
MEDICAL.question: Is it legal for medical marijuana patients to possess cannabis in the state of New Hampshire?
MEDICAL.gov_section: There is a 2 ounce possession limit per patient, and all patients are limited to purchasing 2 ounces of cannabis in any 10-day period.

sourceNotes: This pass started from https://www.nh.gov/ on 2026-09-08. That homepage is the state portal and does not itself describe cannabis law. Its agency directory links to the Department of Health and Human Services at https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/, and the dedicated program is the Therapeutic Cannabis Program at https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/programs-services/population-health/therapeutic-cannabis. Every cited row in this file comes from that DHHS page. The older sentence that recreational cannabis use remains prohibited is gone from the page; RSA 126-X is now described as an exemption from criminal penalties for therapeutic use only, and the page still states a two-ounce patient possession limit, ATC purchase with a registry ID card, and ATC responsibility for cultivation. The prior gc.nh.gov MEDICAL citation was replaced because the requested walk from nh.gov already answers possession on the DHHS page. gc.nh.gov remains the General Court host that www.nh.gov links to, and the same RSAs are official there, but this pass did not need it. A browser-headed fetch of the cited DHHS page returned 200 with the excerpts in the HTML, so these rows do not need a browser.
